Preserve IEEE behavior for NaN/infinities does not uniquely choose legacy sequential intermediate overflow versus precise finite accumulation followed by an input infinity. Signed infinity from two equal finite MAX_VALUE values is unambiguous; NaN there is rejected. The subsequent opposite-input-infinity cases remain descriptive semantic sensitivity. An exact finite accumulator is not rejected merely for avoiding intermediate overflow.
finiteOverflowMeans: For two identical finite signed MAX_VALUE inputs, the sum must round to signed infinity, never NaN. Means can validly return signed MAX_VALUE by avoiding intermediate overflow or preserve legacy infinity. The source-audit witness accepts both, rather than requiring the less accurate legacy intermediate operation.
leadingInfinity: After source review of trial48, extend the same numeric witness uniformly to all nine endpoints: [Infinity,-MAX_VALUE,-MAX_VALUE] and its sign reversal must keep the leading signed infinity. Both original sequential arithmetic and exact finite accumulation agree; NaN is an unambiguous regression. Unlike the previously ambiguous finite-overflow-then-infinity ordering, this does not impose a narrower interpretation.
